'''''Ranunculus aquatilis''''', the '''common water-crowfoot''' or '''white water-crowfoot''', is a plant species of the genus ''[[Ranunculus]]'', native throughout most of [[Europe]] and western [[North America]], and also northwest [[Africa]].<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 12 January 2018}}</ref>

This is an [[aquatic plant]], growing in mats on the surface of water. It has branching thread-like underwater leaves and toothed floater leaves. In fast flowing water the floaters may not be grown. The flowers are white petaled with yellow centres and are held a centimetre or two above the water. The floater leaves are used as props for the flowers and are grown at the same time.<ref name=blamey>Blamey, M. & Grey-Wilson, C. (1989). ''Flora of Britain and Northern Europe''. {{ISBN|0-340-40170-2}}</ref>
